\section{Generated reference tables}\label{sec:gentables}
% ============================================================
%  Wrapper for the machine-generated reference tables.
%
%  Every \input below is produced by scripts/gen_report_tables.py
%  directly from the C++ source tree, so the tables track the code
%  rather than drift from it.  DO NOT edit the generated/*.tex files
%  by hand -- edit the source (or the generator) and re-run:
%
%      python scripts/gen_report_tables.py            # regenerate
%      python scripts/gen_report_tables.py --check    # CI drift guard
%                                                     # (NB: writes before
%                                                     #  it compares)
% ============================================================

The tables in this appendix are generated from the source tree by
\texttt{scripts/gen\_report\_tables.py}.  They are not maintained by hand: a
renamed flag, a new cycle-slip detector, or a changed state-key delimiter
appears here on the next run of the generator.  \emph{Known gap:} the
feature-flag table de-duplicates on the C\texttt{++} member name rather
than on the JSON path, so a section master switch named \texttt{enable}
in more than one config sub-struct appears only once, so several
\texttt{network.*} masters, including those governing the default-off
subsystems this appendix exists to disclose, are consequently absent.
Treat the flag table as indicative and \texttt{GnssConfigLoad.cpp} /
\texttt{GnssConfigLoadNetwork.cpp} as authoritative until
\texttt{gen\_report\_tables.py} keys on the path.  The fragments under
\texttt{generated/} are \texttt{.gitignore}d and rebuilt on demand
(\texttt{build.ps1 -Regen} / \texttt{build.sh -{}-regen}); to see whether
anything moved, re-run the generator and check \texttt{git status}
(\texttt{-{}-check} is not read-only, since it rewrites the fragments before
comparing them).
